dependency_check.status: Active OWASP Flagship-adjacent project; maintained by volunteers with constrained capacity
dependency_check.nvd_api_key_issue: NVD 2.0 API is the only feed. Without an NVD API key v12.2.x hits HTTP 429 rate limits, retries 30+ times and can corrupt the H2 database (GitHub issue #8298). Treat the key as mandatory; cache the DB centrally (shared volume or internal mirror) and update once per day rather than per build.
dependency_check.how_team_should_use: Keep only as a free baseline in Java/Maven CI where no commercial SCA exists; do not position as primary SCA in client proposals. Prefer OSV-Scanner or Trivy for new pipelines and feed results into Dependency-Track.

dependency_track.latest_version: 5.0 GA (9 June 2026); 4.13.x remains on LTS-style maintenance
dependency_track.features: Continuous SBOM analysis (NVD, OSV, GitHub Advisories, Snyk, Trivy, EPSS), CEL expression policies, component hash integrity checks against typosquatting, horizontal scaling on PostgreSQL, durable execution engine, VEX/VDR, portfolio dashboards, notifications; v5 needs offline migration from v4
dependency_track.how_team_should_use: Standard SBOM operations platform for client engagements with CRA, EO 14028 or NIS2 obligations. Ingest CycloneDX from Syft/Trivy/commercial SCA, apply policies, produce VEX. Plan v4 to v5 migration windows for existing deployments.

cyclonedx.relationship: OWASP CycloneDX is the ECMA-424 standardised BOM format (SBOM, SaaSBOM, HBOM, ML-BOM/AI-BOM, CBOM, VEX, VDR). Dependency-Track consumes CycloneDX natively; Snyk aibom, Trivy, Syft, GitLab and most commercial SCA export CycloneDX 1.6.
cyclonedx.how_team_should_use: Mandate CycloneDX 1.6 as the exchange format in delivery standards; require AI-BOM (ML-BOM) sections for client applications embedding models or LLM SDKs.

scvs.name: OWASP Software Component Verification Standard (SCVS) v1.0
scvs.summary: Six control families (Inventory, SBOM, Build Environment, Package Management, Component Analysis, Pedigree and Provenance) at three levels; complements SLSA and SSDF.
scvs.how_team_should_use: Use SCVS as the maturity yardstick in AppSec assessments and RFP responses; map tool capabilities (reachability, provenance, SBOM lifecycle) to SCVS levels to justify tooling choices.

top10_2025_a03.name: OWASP Top 10:2025 A03 Software Supply Chain Failures (final release)
top10_2025_a03.summary: Expands the former A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components / 2013 A9 into build, distribution and update-process compromises. Mapped CWEs: 447, 1035, 1104, 1329, 1357, 1395. Guidance: SBOMs, continuous inventory, trusted sources, staged rollouts, CI/CD change tracking, hardened build systems, patch management.
top10_2025_a03.how_team_should_use: Re-baseline client AppSec programmes against A03: SCA alone is insufficient; add ingestion-time blocking (Firewall/Curation), provenance (SLSA, Sigstore), pipeline hardening and SBOM lifecycle. Use A03 language in executive briefings to justify supply chain budget.

market_trends_2025_2026: Reachability is table stakes: Endor Labs, Semgrep, Socket, Aikido, Xygeni, Arnica and Checkmarx all ship it; Cycode and Konvu push beyond to AI exploitability analysis. Buyers now ask for language coverage and accuracy benchmarks rather than whether it exists.

Malicious package surge: Shai-Hulud worm (Sept 2025, 500+ npm packages incl. CrowdStrike-published packages), Shai-Hulud 2.0 (Nov 2025), CHAINDROP (400+ packages), Axios and LiteLLM compromises (Mar 2026), TanStack/Mistral mass campaign and continued npm/PyPI waves through July 2026. Install-time blocking (Repository Firewall, JFrog Curation, Veracode Package Firewall, Socket Firewall, Endor Package Firewall, Aikido Safe Chain, SafeDep PMG) moved from optional to mandatory.

AI-generated dependency hallucination (slopsquatting): CSA research note (Apr 2026) and vendor studies cite up to 27% hallucinated package names from LLMs; Sonatype Guide MCP (Mar 2026), SafeDep MCP, Socket and Snyk Studio insert verified-package checks into coding agents.

Agent-era supply chain: MCP servers, agent skills and IDE extensions are the new attack surface. JFrog AI Catalog/Agent Guard (Sept 2026), Snyk agent-scan, Endor AURI, AIR ($50M, Sept 2026) target it. AI-BOM (CycloneDX 1.6 ML-BOM) support arriving from Snyk, Mend AI, Black Duck AI Model Risk Insights, Sonatype, JFrog.

Leaders publicly confirmed: Black Duck, Checkmarx, JFrog, Sonatype, Cycode, Chainguard. Visionaries: Endor Labs, Lineaje, ReversingLabs. Also recognised: RapidFort, Arnica. SCA is now evaluated as one pillar alongside SBOM lifecycle, third-party binary analysis and threat intelligence.

Consolidation into ASPM/platforms: Snyk, Checkmarx One, Cycode, Aikido, Arnica, Xygeni, Mend and Veracode Risk Manager sell SCA as a module; pure-play SCA buying is declining except for licence/SBOM specialists (FOSSA) and hardened-source vendors (Chainguard, Echo).
